# 楞嚴經序指味疏

**ID:** X0313
**Volume:** X16

**Original Category:** 大小乘釋經部／方等部疏
**Byline:** 清 諦閑述
**Dynasty:** 清
**Date:** 1644–1911
**Juans:** 1
**CBETA:** https://cbetaonline.dila.edu.tw/zh/X0313

## Contributors
- 諦閑 (A001825)

## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

A one-fascicle (1卷) **Tiāntái-school commentary** by **Dìxián Gǔxū** 諦閑古虛 [諦閑](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%AB%A6%E9%96%91) (1858–1932) on the **prefatory section** alone of the *Śūraṃgama-sūtra* ([KR6j0118](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6j/KR6j0118)). The author identifies himself as *Huángyán Táizōng yìsūn bǐqiū Dìxián shùshū* 黃巖台宗裔孫比丘諦閑述疏 ("monk Dìxián, lineal heir of the Tiāntái school in Huángyán, composed the commentary"), with a colophon by his disciple [華山](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%8F%AF%E5%B1%B1) Huāshān. Preserved as **X16 no. 313** in the *Xùzàngjīng*. The title's metaphor — *zhǐwèi* 指味, "pointing to the flavour" — signals an exegesis that aims to bring out the doctrinal taste of the prefatory section rather than analyze it line by line.

**Abstract**

The work is the most prominent late-Qīng Tiāntái-school treatment of the *Śūraṃgama* prefatory section: the author limits himself to the opening *xù* 序 (the canonical narrative of the sūtra's setting, audience, and *yīnyuán* causation), reading it through a fivefold *jiětí* 解題 system (合釋 / 離釋 / 釋別題 [釋大佛頂 / 釋首楞嚴] / 釋通題) and then through a four-part *shìwén* 釋文 covering the *yījīng dàzhǐ* 一經大旨 ("cardinal purport of the entire sūtra"), the *shízhóu wényì* 十軸文義 ("textual sense of the ten fascicles"), the *míngyì yīnguǒ* 名義因果 ("naming-and-meaning, cause-and-effect"), and the *lǐxíng xìngxiū* 理行性修 ("principle/practice, nature/cultivation"). The work is firmly within the Tiāntái-school tradition begun by [子璿](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%AD%90%E7%92%BF) Chángshuǐ Zǐxuán in the Sòng and continued by [靈耀](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%9D%88%E8%80%80) Língyào in the early Qīng (whose *Guānxīn dìngjiě* [KR6j0714](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6j/KR6j0714) Dìxián studied), but represents a more concentrated and pedagogical late-Qīng restatement. Composition: 1893; editorial preparation through 1902.
